senses.gloss: (cmp. בָּקַר, a preced. wds.) [to break through; cmp. פָּרַץ,]

units: <cite ref="Megillah 25b:12">Meg. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>מתוך תשובה</he> … <he>פָּקְרוּ המינים</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>המערערים</he>) from the answer which Aaron gave to Moses (<cite ref="Exodus 32:24">Ex. XXXII, 24</cite>) the heretics derived their heresy (to assert the reality of idolatrous witchcraft).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 38b:14">Snh. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>כל מקום שפקרו המינין וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>הצדוקים</he>) wherever in a Biblical passage the heretics seem to find a support for their scepticism (belief in a plurality of divine beings), their refutation is always near by; Y. Ber. IX, 12ᵈ bot. (not <he>שפרקו</he>); a. e.

senses.gloss: (with עַצְמ־) to make free with one’s self; (of a woman) to propose marriage to a man.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:3:9">Y. Snh. II, 20ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 25:31">I Sam. XXV, 31</cite> <he>וזכרת את אמתך</he>) <he>מלמד שפָּקְרָה עצמה</he> this shows that she intimated eventual marriage to David; a. e.

senses.gloss: to declare free, to renounce ownership, declare a property ownerless.
units: <cite ref="Gittin 38a">Gitt. 38ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>המַפְקִיר עבדו יצא לחירות</he> if one declares his slave ownerless, he goes out free (and needs no letter of emancipation); <cite ref="Gittin 39a:12">ib. 39ᵃ</cite> <he>המפקיר … וצריך וכ׳</he> he is entitled to his liberty, but requires a letter of emancipation.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 224:4">Yalk. Kings 224</cite> <he>ה׳ כל אשר לו</he> (not <cite ref="Q01449"><he>הפקיד</he></cite>) he gave up all he possessed. Tanḥ. Pinḥas 2 <he>בת מלך הִפְקִירוּ לקלון</he> they offered a king’s daughter to prostitution; <he>ה׳ בתו מי לא היה מפקיר</he> he (the king) offered his daughter, who would not do the same?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 6:1">Peah VI, 1</cite> <he>עד שיוּפְקַר וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>שיבקר</he>, read as <cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 4:3">Eduy. IV, 3</cite> <he>שׁיוּבְקַר</he>) until it is declared free also for rich men; a. e.—Part. pass. <he>מוּפְקָר</he>; f. <he>מוּפְקֶרֶת</he>; pl. <he>מוּפְקָרִים</he>, <he>מוּפְקָרִין</he>; <he>מוּפְקָרוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 49a:16">Snh. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>מה מדבר מ׳ לכל אף ביתו … מ׳ לכל</he> as the desert is free to all, so was Joab’s house free to all (that craved his hospitality). Tanḥ. Vayaḳhel 8 <he>למה … מה המדבר מ׳ … התורה מ׳ וכ׳</he> why was the Law given in the desert? To intimate that as the desert is free to all, so are the words of the Law free to every one &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 72">Gen. R. s. 72</cite> <he>דבר שהוא מן המ׳</he> something which is free (ownerless); a. fr.—V. <cite ref="E00759"><he>הֶפְקֵר</he></cite>.
